title: In Conversation: Founder James on His Favourite Things, and Why Play Beats Discipline
dek: It is the founder’s birthday, so we asked him the questions learners never get to ask: what he actually loves about language, which structures he reaches for first, and why the learners who play out loud overtake the ones who study hardest.

blocks.text: October is the founder’s edition, and it is also James’s birthday month. So this issue does something the magazine rarely does: it gets personal. Instead of asking how to learn, we asked what he loves — the structures, the sounds, the small rituals — and let the method explain itself from there. The theme of the volume is playfulness: conversational agility, the courage to speak a messy draft out loud, and the strange fact that learners who allow themselves to be silly progress faster than learners who are careful.
blocks.say: October is the founder’s edition, and it is also James’s birthday month. So this issue does something the magazine rarely does: it gets personal. Instead of asking how to learn, we asked what he loves.

blocks.text: This Month: JY DM’s Birthday & His Favs
blocks.say: This Month: JY DM’s Birthday & His Favs

blocks.text: Vol. 2026.10 opens with a practical gift: ten reusable sentence frames, in fourteen languages, that let you speak from the first day without translating in your head. The COSYtalks piece then asks the question underneath the frames — why do we freeze the moment a conversation leaves the script? — and the Grammar desk closes with the founder’s own five favourite rules, chosen because they unlock the most speech for the least effort.
Playfulness is the thread. Every piece in this issue assumes you will say something wrong, and treats that as the point rather than the cost.
